headline: Broad Rally Caps a Record Options Week; Hormuz Tensions and Fed Timing Set the Agenda
body_html:
Friday's session closed out a remarkable stretch for equities, with 414 of 549 names in our universe finishing higher and every major sector in the green except Energy, which shed 0.54%. Semiconductors led the advance at plus 3.81%, followed by Homebuilders at 2.62% and Software at 2.32%. The broad participation underscored a market that, per reporting, just logged a record-breaking week for options activity while its volatility gauge settled near a 2026 low.

The session's sharpest individual moves reflected a busy earnings backdrop. Corsair Gaming surged 35.25%, Twilio added 24.89%, and Natera climbed 21.37%, each appearing to react to company-specific results or guidance. On the downside, Trade Desk dropped 21.90%, the steepest single-name decline in the session, while Akamai fell 6.76% and ResMed gave back 5.06%. Energy-services name Innovex International lost 8.47% as crude-supply uncertainty weighed on the sub-sector.

Heading into the new week, traders will be navigating a dense geopolitical calendar alongside fresh macro data. The Strait of Hormuz standoff remains unresolved — a UAE vessel was struck by an Iranian missile and re-opening conditions are still disputed — while a softer-than-expected U.S. jobs print pushed out expectations for a Federal Reserve rate move, sending the dollar lower. How those two threads develop will likely set the tone through Friday.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Impasse Deepens After Vessel Strike
briefs.body: The UAE reported that an Iranian missile struck an ADNOC-affiliated ship in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating an already fragile situation. Iran's Revolutionary Guard simultaneously signaled that reopening the waterway is not contingent on talks with Oman, complicating diplomatic pathways. Energy markets will be watching tanker-traffic data closely at the open.

briefs.headline: Weak Jobs Print Reshapes Fed Rate Expectations
briefs.body: Softer U.S. employment figures released Friday prompted traders to push back their timeline for the next Federal Reserve rate increase, according to Reuters. The dollar fell in response, offering a tailwind to commodity prices and multinational earnings. Fed speakers on this week's calendar will be closely parsed for any course-correction signals.

briefs.headline: Sunni Defense Pact Raises Regional Stakes
briefs.body: Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia announced a mutual-defense arrangement carrying obligations technically equivalent to NATO's Article 5, a Turkish minister confirmed. The pact adds a new layer of complexity to Middle East risk calculus just as Hormuz negotiations remain unresolved. Investors in regional energy and defense-adjacent names are reassessing exposure accordingly.

briefs.headline: Senate Advances Russia Sanctions Package
briefs.body: The U.S. Senate passed a Russia sanctions bill championed by Senator Graham, sending the legislation to the House for consideration. If enacted, the measures could affect commodity flows and multinational operating environments across several sectors. The timing — amid elevated geopolitical tension elsewhere — adds to a crowded risk calendar for the week ahead.

briefs.headline: Twilio Surges Nearly 25% on Earnings Catalyst
briefs.body: Cloud-communications platform Twilio posted the second-largest single-session gain in Friday's universe, jumping 24.89% in a move consistent with a well-received quarterly report. The advance lifted the broader Software sector, which finished up 2.32% and ranked third among all groups. Analysts will parse the earnings call transcript over the weekend for forward-guidance detail.

briefs.headline: Trade Desk Suffers Sharpest Decline of the Session
briefs.body: Ad-technology firm Trade Desk fell 21.90%, the steepest drop across our entire tracked universe on Friday, suggesting a significant earnings or guidance disappointment. The selloff dragged on internet-infrastructure peers and highlighted divergent fortunes within the broader technology complex. Investors will be watching whether the weakness attracts dip-buying or continued distribution when markets reopen Monday.
